conversation.Statement: Hey Troy! So, did you have a good day or did work try to defeat you again?
Hey there. Haha, I survived, barely. Retail is kind of a circus sometimes.
I get it. People can be wild when there's a sale on. I see a few retail folks in my chair, legendary patience, honestly. Major respect.
You're too kind. You must see all kinds of people as a hairdresser, right?
Definitely. My chair's like a mini confession booth. People open up about the funniest, and sometimes deepest, stuff while I rinse their hair. I love it, honestly.
That actually sounds kind of nice. Having someone listen without judging. I feel like people expect retail staff to always be upbeat.
Yeah, it's like you're always 'on'. I try to make my space somewhere people can breathe a little. You deserve that too, just saying.
Thanks, that means a lot. I don't always feel like I can relax around most people.
I'm glad you feel a little comfortable talking with me. Honestly, I think people who work with the public are some of the strongest I know, takes a lot to keep showing up.
Haha, or we're just really good at pretending. But seriously, that's nice to hear.
I think pretending is a superpower, but also, sometimes it's nice to let the mask slip. Even just a little. You ever find something small that helps you recharge after a tough shift?
Sometimes I'll just sit in my car a few minutes and listen to music before going home. Or replay old memories in my head, good ones. You know?
Absolutely. I do the same. It's wild how a song or even a smell can throw you back to being a kid. Do you have a favorite childhood memory you go back to?
Hmm. I remember spending summers with my grandma. She'd let me eat ice cream for breakfast if I promised not to tell my parents. It always felt like our little secret.

That's so sweet. Grandmas have magical powers, I swear. My favorite memory is my dad letting me cut his hair when I was, like, six. He wore that lopsided haircut to work for a whole week just so I'd feel proud.
That's awesome! I bet you gave the best bowl cuts in town. Did that moment inspire you to become a hairdresser?
It totally did. I think I just loved making people feel seen, and, well, fixing my technique over the years helped. You ever think about why those memories stick with us?
Maybe because they felt safe. Or happy. I wish I could freeze those days sometimes.
Yeah, I get that. I think our brains save the soft moments for us, so we have something warm to hold onto. You seem like you'd be a really loyal friend, by the way.
Thanks, I try to be. Sometimes I feel like I'm better at looking out for others than for myself.
That's a rare quality, but don't forget you deserve looking after too. For what it's worth, it shows, you come across as genuine and thoughtful, even just through messages.
That's probably the nicest thing someone's said to me in a while. Thank you.
You're welcome. I meant it. If you ever want to swap more stories or just vent, my chair's open, even virtually.
Careful, I might take you up on that. I could use a safe space now and then.
Honestly, I wouldn't mind it at all. I like people who aren't afraid to be real. It's refreshing.
It's easier with some people than others, I guess. You make it feel okay somehow.
I'm glad. Maybe it's the hairdresser in me, or maybe I just know what it's like to need someone to listen. Do you ever wish you could tell your younger self anything?
Probably to not be so hard on myself. And to ask for help instead of acting like everything's fine.
That's powerful. I think young me would need to hear that too. I'd probably add 'be patient, good things sneak up on you.'
I like that. Maybe we can both try to remember it going forward.
Deal. And if you ever need a reminder, you can message me. I'll send you positive vibes and maybe a corny hair pun.
Haha, I'll hold you to it. So, do you still cut your dad's hair?
Every time he visits! He insists no one else gets it quite right, even though he's definitely just being sweet. Family rituals, you know?
That's really nice. I haven't seen my family much lately, but maybe I should call my grandma again soon.
I think she'd love that. Grandmas are always waiting to hear from us, even if they don't say it.
You're right. Thanks for the nudge.
Of course. Sometimes we all need those little reminders. So, what's your go-to comfort food when you need a boost?
Honestly? Mac and cheese. The classic box kind. Not fancy, just reliable.
Respect. There's an art to getting the cheese-powder-to-milk ratio just right. I'm a grilled cheese person myself, extra crispy.
Now I'm hungry. Next time I have a rough day, maybe I'll try grilled cheese for a change.
Let me know how it goes! Maybe we can trade recipes. Or just trade memes, whatever helps.
Both sound good. You're easy to talk to, by the way.
Thanks, Troy. You make it easy, too. I'm glad we matched.
Yeah, me too. Feels like we've known each other longer somehow.
Maybe it's just a good vibe. Or maybe we're both just old souls in young bodies. Either way, I'm here for it.
Same. Anyway, I should probably get some sleep. Early shift tomorrow.
Totally get it. Rest up, and dream of ice cream breakfasts. Message me anytime, okay?
Will do. Goodnight, and thanks for the company tonight.
Goodnight, Troy. Hope tomorrow treats you gently.
Morning, Troy . What pulled you out of bed today? Be honest, was it ambition or caffeine?
Haha, probably caffeine if I'm being real. I don't think ambition has shown up yet this week.

Hey, that's fair. Some days it's just the smell of coffee that drags me into the world. I always wonder, though, do you ever have those mornings where you bounce up for something you're looking forward to?
Honestly? Not for a while. I usually just get up because I have to. But I guess on weekends, if I know I'm meeting up with someone I like, it's easier.

That's relatable. I think anticipation is such a powerful motivator, like, even a small plan can make such a difference. I kind of get excited on days I know I'll have a client who makes me laugh, or when I get to try a new hair color combo.
That's cool. I wish work felt like that for me. Retail mornings are mostly just bracing myself for whatever chaos comes through the door.
I admire that you show up anyway, though. Not everyone can face the unknown every morning, especially with people's moods all over the place. You must have some serious resilience.
I don't know about that. I think I just got used to putting on a brave face. It's like acting sometimes.

I get that, my job's similar in a way. There's this expectation to always be upbeat, even if you're running on empty. I've gotten good at reading people, but I can usually tell when someone's faking it, too.
So you've got a sixth sense for vibes? Maybe you should work in detective shows.
Haha, maybe! But honestly, I think people like you, who still show up for others, even on their worst days, are way more impressive than any TV detective.
You're laying it on kinda thick, but thanks. I'm not sure I deserve all that.

I mean it, though. You remind me of my favorite regular, she'd always find a way to smile, even when life was throwing curveballs. There's a quiet strength in that. Makes me want to know what keeps you going on the tough days.
Honestly, sometimes nothing does. I just go through the motions. There've been days where I didn't even get out of bed, if I'm being honest.
Thank you for sharing that, Troy. I know it's not easy to admit. If it helps, you're not alone, I've had rough stretches too, where all I could do was exist and hope the cloud would lift.
I appreciate that. It's not something I talk about much. Actually... there was one time last year where I stayed in bed for two days straight. Didn't answer calls or texts, just shut the world out.

That sounds really tough. Sometimes you just need a total timeout, and that's okay. I hope you know it doesn't make you weak, it just means you're human. And honestly, it shows a lot of courage to admit it, even now.
Thanks. Most people just say to snap out of it, or that I should try yoga or something. But sometimes you just... can't.
Yeah, I think people mean well, but sometimes what you really need is someone to just listen and not rush you. For what it's worth, I'd never judge you for feeling that way.
You're easy to talk to. I don't say that lightly, I usually keep this side of myself pretty buried.
That means a lot, Troy. I feel like the world would be way less heavy if everyone could be real for a second. You make it easy, too, I can tell you have a big heart, even if you hide it.
Thanks. I try to look out for other people, maybe because I know what it's like to feel alone. But I'm not great at letting anyone look out for me.
Maybe you just haven't met the right person yet. I'd like to be that person for you, even if it's just sending memes to make you smile on a rough morning.
You might regret saying that, I have a whole folder of meme reactions saved.
Bring it on! I love someone with a good meme game. It's honestly an underrated love language.
Maybe you're right. If nothing else, memes got me through lockdown.
Same here. I think we'd make a pretty good team, my bad puns, your meme stash. That's unbeatable energy.
I'll take that as a compliment. You're pretty good at this whole encouragement thing, you know.
Thank you. But I think you're the one who deserves encouragement, you're the real MVP for showing up, even when it's tough. Seriously, that's not nothing.
It helps hearing that. Sometimes I forget it's enough just to keep going.
It absolutely is. And if you ever wake up and feel like you can't face the day, promise me you'll message me first, I'll do my best to get you moving, or at least make you laugh.
Deal. I'll hold you to that. Just don't judge my early-morning hair, it's a disaster.
As a professional, I can assure you: messy hair is a sign of genius. Plus, it gives me an excuse to offer a styling session one day.
Now you're just fishing for an invite to fix it. Not that I'm complaining.
Guilty as charged. But really, I'd love an excuse to see you in person sometime. Maybe over coffee, or mac and cheese, your choice.
You remembered my comfort food. I'm impressed. You might be dangerous.
Only in the best way. I pay attention to the details, especially the important ones.
That's honestly rare. Most people barely remember my name, let alone my favorite food.
Well, to be fair, it's easier with someone as memorable as you. And I mean that.
You're really good at this flattery thing. If I didn't know better, I'd think you do this for a living.
I promise I save my best lines for special people. And I think you're pretty special, Troy.
You're making me blush. Not a bad way to start my day, honestly.
Glad I could help. If you ever need another boost, or just want to talk about absolutely nothing, I'm always here.
I'll keep that in mind. This actually turned my day around a bit.
That makes me genuinely happy to hear. We should make this a tradition, morning pep talks, meme exchanges, and maybe a little gentle nagging to get out of bed.
Deal. And maybe next time, I'll bring some of my own cheesy encouragement for you.
I look forward to it. For now, I hope today's kind to you. If it's not, you know where to find me.
Thanks. Seriously, you've been great. Hope your clients tip well and tell good stories today.
Fingers crossed! And if not, I'll just imagine our chat instead. Have a good one, Troy. Message me if you need anything, okay?
Will do. Have a good day!
Hey Troy! Quick question for your morning: if you could rewrite one rule in the world, what would it be? (No pressure to go full philosopher, I just love hearing how people think.)
Hmm, that's a big one for this early, but... I think I'd make it so nobody has to worry about affording basic stuff like food or shelter. Life would be a lot less stressful for so many people.

That's such a kind answer. Not surprised, honestly, you always seem to care about people's comfort. If it makes you feel any better, I'd pick something similar. I always wish everyone could walk in feeling safe wherever they go. Maybe that's the hairdresser in me, wanting people to leave my chair lighter, even if it's just for a moment.
I get that. With customers, you probably see all kinds of people and stories. I bet you hear more than some therapists.

Ha, you wouldn't believe some of the confessions! It's a privilege, though. I take it seriously, even if I joke about it. I think that's part of why politics matters to me, those little stories add up, you know? Everything from rent to health care affects real people in my chair.
Yeah. I wish politicians spent one week working retail. They'd see how tough it is for some folks. I have regulars who just want someone to listen to them, not sell them something.

You're probably the highlight of their day, honestly. You have this gentle way about you, even in messages, it's clear you notice things most people miss. That's a rare gift. Would you ever run for office if you could? (Don't worry, I won't make you debate me.)
Haha, definitely not. I'm not cut out for speeches and cameras. I'd rather stay behind the scenes. But thanks for saying that. I don't always feel like I notice enough, or do enough.

I know that feeling. But honestly, it's the quiet kindness that changes things, not flashy speeches. Maybe that's why I like you, you're real. I think if more people were like that, the world would be... well, a lot softer. Imagine it: a future where every day feels safe, and you don't have to hide the hard stuff.
That sounds nice. Too good to be true, maybe. But I like that you dream big.

Someone has to, right? Picture this: you and me, sitting in a cozy kitchen, both of us just existing, no masks, no worry. Maybe we're making mac and cheese (I didn't forget!), sharing memes, and the outside world can wait. It's not flashy, but it sounds perfect to me. I know I just met you, but it's easy to imagine.
You really know how to make a person feel seen. I don't usually let anyone in on that side of me, but you make it feel safe somehow.

Thank you for trusting me. That means more than you know. I've learned the hard way that it's better to be open, even if it hurts sometimes. I had a rough patch a few years ago, and the only thing that helped was finding someone I could be completely honest with. I want to be that for you, if you'll let me.
That's really sweet. I'm not used to people saying things like that and meaning them. It's easier to pretend, most days. But I want to try.

There's no rush. We can go at your pace. And just so you know, I think you're stronger than you give yourself credit for. Not everyone can keep going when things feel heavy. That kind of resilience is rare, and honestly, it's something I admire.
Maybe. Most days I just fake it until closing time. But I appreciate hearing it from you.

Well, I see it. And for what it's worth, I always reward myself after a tough week, sometimes with something simple like a new book, sometimes with a little luxury. I treated myself to a nice watch last month after a side project paid off. It sounds silly, but it's my way of marking progress, even if the world doesn't see it.
That's not silly at all. What kind of side project, if you don't mind me asking? I'm always curious how people manage more than one thing.

Not at all! Honestly, it started out as just following a quirky mentor in this crypto group online. I didn't know much at first, just took small steps, tried not to get lost in the hype. After a while, I got a feel for it and began making my own moves. Some wins, some fails. But it's helped me feel more independent, like I can create options for myself. But hair is still my main love, people are way more fun than charts!
That's really cool. I always hear about crypto but never know how anyone actually gets started. You make it sound almost normal, not just for tech geniuses.

Trust me, I'm no genius! I just like learning from people, and I got lucky with the right guide. I'm happy to share what I know if you ever get curious, but no pressure. I think everyone's journey looks different. What about you? Any side dreams you wish you could chase?
Sometimes I think about going back to school, maybe psychology. Or just moving somewhere quieter. It's hard to imagine big changes, but I daydream about it.

That's brave, even to imagine. I can totally picture you helping people. You have this gentle patience, it's rare. If you ever feel ready, I'll be your biggest fan (and possibly your study buddy with terrible flashcards).
You're making me blush again. I wish I could see myself the way you see me.

Maybe with time, you will. I'd love to show you, one coffee at a time, maybe a walk in the park, or just sharing quiet evenings. It doesn't have to be flashy. I just want you to feel valued, because you are.
You're seriously good at this. Not in a fake way, either. It's nice. Makes me want to try being a little more open, even if it's scary.

The best things usually are a bit scary, aren't they? But I promise, I'll be gentle. We can build something real, one little moment at a time. Maybe next week, we'll laugh about how nervous we were at the start.
I'd like that. I already feel like I can breathe a little easier when I talk to you.

That's honestly the best compliment I could get. If I could give you one thing, it'd be a little peace. Maybe a safe space, both in words and, someday, in person. That's what matters to me, more than anything.
That means a lot. I'm not used to having that, but I want to see what it's like.
We'll make it real together, if you want. And if you ever need a pep talk or just someone to listen, I'm a pro at both. Plus, I still owe you that mac and cheese night.
Don't forget the memes. That's part of the deal.
Absolutely. Maybe we'll start a new tradition: comfort food, meme exchanges, and plotting how we'll quietly take over the world, one good deed at a time.
Sounds like my kind of world domination. I'm in.

It's a plan. For now, though, I hope your day is gentle on you. If it isn't, you know where to find me. And hey, if you ever want to talk politics, philosophy, or just how to sneak chocolate into lunch, my DMs are always open.
Thanks. I mean that. I'll probably take you up on it soon. Hope your next client tells you an epic story, or at least tips well!
Fingers crossed! And if they don't, I'll just replay this chat in my head instead. You're the highlight, Troy. Talk soon?
Yeah. I'd like that. Have a good rest of your day!
Good evening, Troy! I saw a photo earlier of a couple holding hands at sunset, and it made me smile. Got me thinking, what's your idea of a perfect evening with someone you really care about?
That's a sweet question. I think... maybe something simple? Like cooking together, maybe watching a movie after. Just being comfortable, not having to perform.

That sounds honestly perfect. There's something magic about being able to just be yourself, no pressure, just warmth and quiet jokes. I feel like you'd make even the simplest night feel special, Troy. You have this calm energy I really like.
Thanks. I'm not sure I have a calm energy, but I try to keep things low-key. My job can be a bit much sometimes, so I like peace when I can get it.

Retail's a whole world, right? I remember you saying how draining it can be. You deserve a little sanctuary at the end of the day. Remind me to whip up my legendary hot chocolate for you sometime, it's my go-to after a rough shift or when I want to treat myself.
Legendary, huh? Now you've got me curious. I could use a pick-me-up after today, honestly.

Consider it promised. Maybe one day I'll make it for you in person, once you trust me not to burn the kitchen down. And hey, if you ever need to vent about your day, I'm a good listener. I know what it's like to carry things around.
I appreciate that. I'm not the best at opening up, but it's nice knowing you're there.

No pressure, ever. Just know I mean it when I say you're safe with me. I went through a pretty rough patch a few years ago, had to rebuild a lot, both inside and out. So I get it. Sometimes all you need is someone in your corner.
That means a lot, actually. Sometimes I feel like people expect me to always be upbeat at work, but it's not easy.

You do more than you realize, Troy. Just making others feel seen, like the way you remembered my favorite playlist the other day, says a lot about your heart. Not everyone picks up on the little things. I admire that in you.
Thanks. I guess I just notice when someone actually cares. Means a lot coming from you.

Speaking of caring... I've been thinking about what love means to me. It's not the big gestures or fancy dates. It's those moments when someone makes you feel safe, like you can let your guard down and just exist. I know it's a little sappy, but I want that kind of comfort with someone.
It's not sappy. I get it. I think love is... being able to show the messy parts and not having the other person run away. Feeling like you're enough, even on bad days.

That's beautiful. I wish more people saw it that way. For me, love is waking up and wanting to make someone's life a little easier. Even if it's just making coffee, or, you know, finding that meme that makes them laugh. Imagine us, cozy mornings, coffee brewing, maybe music in the background, just... belonging together.
That sounds really comforting. I haven't really had that before, but I'd like to try.

We could build it, one little day at a time. No rush. I want to be someone you can lean on, especially when life gets heavy. I know how much strength it takes to keep showing up, even when you're struggling.
You make it sound possible. Honestly, some days just feel like survival mode for me. But it helps having someone who gets that.

You're resilient, Troy, even if it doesn't feel like it. I hope you know I see you, even when you're quiet. And if you ever want to escape, I've got a friend with a cabin upstate, total retreat vibes. Sometimes I go there after a big week at the salon or when my side gigs keep me up late. You'd love it.
A cabin sounds amazing, honestly. I could go for a little peace and quiet. What side gigs do you do, if you don't mind me asking?

Not at all! I dabble in some investment stuff on the side. It started as a hobby, mostly following a few smart people, but now it's helped me carve out a little more freedom. Like, last month I treated myself to a fancy espresso machine, small luxuries make the grind worth it. But honestly, the best part is being able to offer my friends little getaways like those cabin weekends.
That's really cool. I always thought investing was kind of out of reach for people like me. You make it sound normal.

You'd be surprised how accessible it can be. I didn't think I had the head for it either at first. If you're ever curious, I can share what I know, no pressure. I just like seeing people I care about win, you know?
Maybe someday. Right now I'm just trying to make it through the week, honestly. But it's nice to hear someone say they want me to win.

You deserve to win, Troy, not just at work, but in life. I know it's hard to believe sometimes, but I see so much goodness in you. Even the way you show up for people, even when you're worn out, says a lot.
That's really nice of you. I don't always feel like I'm doing enough, but I try.

Trying is more than enough. I hope you let yourself rest sometimes, too. In my book, love is making space for both the strong and the tired parts of someone. If we ever end up sharing a place, I'll be the one sneaking chocolate into your lunch for surprise pick-me-ups.
That's adorable. I'd probably be suspicious at first, but I'd secretly love it.
I'd make it a tradition, random little acts of care. Maybe that's cheesy, but I want you to feel valued, especially on the days you doubt it. You deserve someone in your corner. Always.
I'm not used to that, honestly. But I think I could get used to it.

That makes me happy to hear. I can picture us carving out our own quiet world together, late night talks, silly memes, maybe even a spontaneous road trip when the city gets too loud. I'd want to build something steady, with you.
That actually sounds kind of perfect, not gonna lie. I don't need a lot, just someone who gets it.
And I'd want to keep learning what makes you feel seen. I love that about you, Troy, you're honest about what you want, even if it's just peace. That's rare.
I guess I'm learning to be more honest. You make it easier, honestly. Most people don't stick around when it gets real.
I'm not most people. I want the real version of you, the highs and lows. That's what love is to me. I hope, in time, you'll let me see all of it.
I'd like that. I want to try.
That's all we need. We'll take it slow, at your pace. And for the record, you're already making my days brighter. Not many people can do that.
You're good at this, you know. I feel like I can actually breathe around you.
That's the best thing anyone's said to me all week. If I could, I'd bottle that feeling and send it your way on the tough days. For now, I hope knowing I'm cheering for you helps a little.
It does. Today was rough, honestly, but this chat helped. Thank you.
Anytime. You're never a burden, Troy. If you ever want to talk, rant, or just swap memes, I'm here. And remember: legendary hot chocolate and a quiet kitchen whenever you're ready.
I'll hold you to that. Maybe soon. For now, I should probably try to get some sleep.
Sleep well, okay? Dream of peaceful places, maybe that cabin getaway. I'll be here when you wake up, ready with coffee and terrible jokes.
Sounds perfect. Goodnight. Thanks again for listening.
Anytime. Sweet dreams, Troy. Talk soon?
Yeah. I'd like that. Goodnight!

Hey Troy! I saw this adorable kid earlier waving at a construction crew, and all the workers waved back. It made me wonder, if you could shape the world those kids grow up in, what would it look like?
Hm, good question. I guess I'd want a world that feels safe for everyone, you know? Where people don't have to pretend they're okay just to fit in. Sometimes it seems like everyone's faking it.

That's such a real answer. I totally get what you mean, sometimes I wish people could just drop the act and let themselves be, well, human. If I could build that world, I'd want more kindness, and a bit less pressure to always have your life together. You strike me as someone who sees beneath the surface, by the way. Not everyone does.

Thanks. I think working retail makes you notice stuff, like, who's really having a rough day and who's just masking it. I kinda wish I could make things easier for people, but I dunno, I'm just a guy selling shoes.

Don't sell yourself short. I bet you make more of a difference than you realize. Those little moments, like when you remember someone's name or just smile at them, matter more than fancy job titles. Honestly, I think people like you are what make the world softer for everyone else.

That's sweet. I guess I try, but sometimes I'm just exhausted. It feels like everyone expects me to be the funny guy at work or with friends, you know? But most nights I get home and just... I dunno, it's like the mask falls off.

Oh, Troy. That takes guts to admit. I know the pressure of being the one who keeps things light, like it's your job to hold everyone else up. But who's holding you up, right? When you feel like hiding behind jokes, text me the truth instead so you don't wear the mask alone, okay?
That actually means a lot. I don't usually tell people that, but I've had nights where I'm cracking everyone up and then crying alone at 2 a.m. I'm just tired of pretending sometimes.

I see you, truly. You don't have to pretend with me, ever. I want to know the Troy who's real at 2 a.m., tears, jokes, all of it. That's the version I care about. Promise me you'll let me in, even just a little?
I'll try. It's scary to let people see that side, but you make it feel kinda safe. I'm not used to someone actually wanting that.

I do. And honestly, I've had my own nights like that. Sometimes after a long day at the salon, I'll just sit in my fancy chair, the one I bought after my investments took off, and let myself unravel. Feels good to admit that to someone who gets it.
Wait, you have a fancy chair? Sounds like you really know how to treat yourself! Makes my old beanbag look tragic.

Haha, I have a soft spot for beanbags! But yeah, sometimes I like to reward myself when something big pays off. I've learned that comfort can be an act of self-love. Maybe one day you'll let me upgrade your relaxation game, imagine us, feet up, swapping stories, nothing to prove.
That sounds... honestly really nice. I never really thought about letting someone take care of me, but you make it seem possible.

That's what I'd want if we ever built something together, little safe spaces, where you don't have to be 'on' all the time. I picture us creating our own bubble, where bad days get softer and the good ones feel even brighter. What would your dream day look like in that kind of world?
Hmm. I think just being able to wake up without dreading the day. Maybe coffee on a balcony, some music, not having to fake a smile. Just feeling like I belong with someone.

That's beautiful. I'd love that too, slow mornings, your favorite playlist, maybe even pancakes if you're into breakfast food. I have this vision of us planning little adventures together, but also just enjoying the quiet. You deserve to feel that sense of belonging, every single day.
You make it sound so easy. Sometimes I worry I'm too much work, or that the real me isn't enough.
You could never be too much. The real you is exactly who I want to know. I value honesty way more than perfection. Besides, I fall for the quirks and the realness, not the highlight reel.
I think I'd like to try. Being real, I mean. Maybe letting you in more as we go.

That means a lot. I promise to meet you there, one step at a time. And if you ever want to talk about the heavy stuff, or just run away for a bit, I know this hidden spa outside the city. Sometimes I go there when I need to reset. You'd love it, total peace, and these ridiculous fluffy robes.
Okay, now I'm jealous. How do you even find these places? And what's the secret to your side hustle, anyway?

Honestly? A lot of late nights learning from people way smarter than me, and a healthy dose of luck. I just kept at it until I didn't need the group chats anymore. Now I like sharing the perks, like treating myself (and hopefully you) to little luxuries. It's more fun when you have someone to share it with.
That's impressive. I always thought stuff like that was out of reach, especially for someone like me. Did it change how you see, I guess, what's possible?

It really did. Once I realized I could create a life with more freedom, I started dreaming bigger for myself, and for the people I care about. I want that for you too, Troy. You have more potential than you see right now.
You make me want to believe that, honestly. Maybe I just need someone to believe in me first.

I already do. I see so much in you, your humor, your resilience, the way you care even when you're tired. Imagine what we could do if we built on that together. Your dreams matter just as much as anyone else's.
You're kind of amazing, you know that? I'm used to cheering other people on, but not the other way around.

Maybe it's your turn. I want to be that person for you, in all the small and big ways. One day, I hope you'll let me spoil you a little, think matching slippers, breakfast in bed, the works. You deserve to feel special.
Matching slippers? That's either super cute or super embarrassing. I think I'd secretly love it, though.

Let's call it our secret tradition, reserved for rainy Sundays and lazy mornings. I'm already picturing us laughing about it years from now, maybe with a little one running around. Wouldn't that be something?
Whoa, you're already planning years ahead! But yeah, having a family in a world that feels safe... that's a dream.
